summary: The result group is the dissection invariance of Hadwiger's codimension-2 invariant in every finite dimension (Hadwiger, Math. Ann. 127, 1954), with the invariant defined from the point set alone. It comes with the invariants of all six regular 4-polytopes and the non-congruence consequences that follow. This is a classical Math. Ann. theorem that founded the higher-dimensional study of Hilbert's third problem. It has a clear specialist audience in scissors congruence and convex geometry: the Dehn–Sydler–Jessen and Dupont–Sah line, and current work on higher scissors congruence. The literature account cites the founding sources precisely, makes no claim of new mathematics or priority, discloses its limits, and reports a reproducible search for prior formalizations. Independent checks found no contradiction.

internal_notes.evidence: Hadwiger 1954; arXiv 1804.09920 excerpt; Wikipedia Dehn invariant
internal_notes.message: Positive. Independent sources confirm that Hadwiger 1954 introduced the d-dimensional invariants and proved them dissection-invariant, and that volume and the invariant form a complete system in dimension 4. Wikipedia credits the dimension-4 completeness to Dupont–Sah 1990, while the submission credits Jessen 1972. Both are standard attributions (Jessen proved it, and Dupont–Sah reworked it homologically). This is not a misattribution.

The paper-worthy core is the bridge: Hadwiger's invariance theorem in every finite dimension, with a set-intrinsic definition that needs no face list as input. Taken alone, the six regular-polytope evaluations and the non-congruence corollaries are routine. Grouped with the bridge, they illustrate it. The audience is geometers working on Hilbert's third problem and scissors congruence, a live area with recent higher-scissors-congruence work by Zakharevich, Malkiewich and others, plus formal-geometry readers. This is narrower than score 5 requires.

Lagarias–Moews show that every polytope that tiles R^n by congruent copies has all its Dehn–Hadwiger invariants zero except volume. That gives the tesseract, 16-cell and 24-cell (all space-fillers) invariant 0 without computation. The 120-cell does not tile, so it needs its own argument (dihedral angle 4π/5). The account cites Lagarias–Moews but does not draw this link. Debrunner 1980 (Arch. Math. 35, 583–587), the 3-dimensional precursor, is omitted. Neither omission changes the public account.

internal_notes.evidence: Submission: every cited source marked 'Not read'
internal_notes.message: The citations are precise, with DOIs and a Zbl number, and the claims they support are standard and confirmed by independent sources. Marking them 'Not read' is honest disclosure, not an unverified claim. Still, an account that rests entirely on bibliographic records is weaker than one that checks the stated content against the papers or a review (MR/Zbl).

The search covers Mathlib and GitHub Lean code and finds no 4-dimensional formalization. My own searches found no Lean, Isabelle or HOL Light formalization of the Dehn or Hadwiger invariant either. The submission discloses that it did not search Isabelle AFP, Rocq, HOL Light or Mizar. That is honest, but it leaves 'no formalization found' scoped to Lean only.

Sanity check: arccos(1/4) ≈ 75.52°, and 240° − 75.52° = 164.48°, which matches the 600-cell's dihedral angle. Both the 5-cell and 600-cell invariants are nonzero real multiples of the same nonzero class [arccos(1/4)], with opposite signs. Since x ↦ x ⊗ θ is injective for θ ≠ 0 over ℚ, no similar copies can match, which agrees with the third non-congruence theorem. No priority is claimed for this, and none was found in the literature searched.
The submitter's earlier 3-dimensional paper resolves and matches the description (published 20 Nov 2026, version DOI ...553). Its provenance is consistent.
Springer full texts (Hadwiger 1954, Lagarias–Moews) were behind a redirect or login. The Encyclopedia of Mathematics page returned HTTP 502 and was used only through a search excerpt.

what_would_reach_higher: Read Hadwiger 1954 (or its Zbl/MR review) and Hadwiger's 1957 Vorlesungen, and state which theorem there is the bridge, with its theorem or page number, instead of 'Not read'.
Give a source for the 'classical' simplex-versus-cube non-congruence for n ≥ 3 (Hadwiger 1954/1957, or Boltianskii, Hilbert's Third Problem, 1978).

Use Lagarias–Moews 1995 (and Debrunner 1980 for dimension 3) to note that the tesseract, 16-cell and 24-cell tile R^4, so their zero invariant is predicted, and that the 120-cell and 600-cell are the non-tiling cases.
Add standard monographs: C.-H. Sah, Hilbert's Third Problem: Scissors Congruence (1979); J. L. Dupont, Scissors Congruences, Group Homology and Characteristic Classes (2001); Boltianskii (1978).
Note that Jessen (1972) and Dupont–Sah (1990) are both credited with the dimension-4 completeness, and say which proves what.
Extend the prior-formalization search to Isabelle AFP, HOL Light, Rocq and Mizar, and record the dates and queries.

To make a stronger case for interest beyond the specialist audience: formalize the identification of the set invariant with Hadwiger's face sum for an arbitrary convex polytope, or Jessen's converse in R^4, which the author lists as not done. Either would make the group a full formal treatment of the 4-dimensional scissors-congruence classification rather than evaluations on six examples.
